source: T-86 frozen T-19 topology (44 children, 22 linked, 36 edges); native fields from task.list/task.view, 2026-10-10. Later unlinked tail items are excluded.

items.title: Repository skeleton and the BCAS hub core extracted

criteria.text: `hub/` builds with Node 24 and TypeScript by type stripping (no build step) and its test suite passes, driving a real spoke and a real hub as BCAS did
No reference to Discord, evidence, boards, slots, SRE or BCAS owner names remains in `hub/`
`cland --version` prints a version from the repo root
`docs/` gains a short `hub/README.md` or equivalent note describing the extracted modules and what was dropped, with a pointer to the BCAS research
Nothing in the repo contains machine paths or secrets

items.title: Per-project hub daemon with discovery and secret

criteria.text: Starting the hub twice in one project is idempotent; the second call reports the running daemon
A spoke connects using only the discovery file and the secret; a wrong secret is refused
The hub outlives the shell that started it; `cland hub status` shows it from a new shell
The volatile files are ignored by git through the managed `.cland/.gitignore`; nothing under `.cland/` other than `tasks/`, `roles.toml`, `config.toml` and `.gitignore` is meant to be committed
Tests start a real hub in a temporary project and connect a real spoke through discovery

items.title: General topic over the UI socket with a minimal Neovim client

criteria.text: General and Agents exist after the first start and cannot be deleted or renamed
A message typed in the Neovim client reaches a test spoke as a `deliver` with topic id and title; its stage shows `queued` while no spoke is connected and `delivered` once a spoke accepts it
A message from the spoke appears in the client's thread within one event round trip, with sender name and time
The same frames work over stdio when the client spawns the hub as a child process (test with a stub hub)
The client loads nothing from the user's own Neovim configuration (`:scriptnames` shows only the bundled runtime and cland's files)
Tests: a real hub plus a scripted UI client over the socket; a headless Neovim driven by `nvim_input` with `screenstring()` asserting the thread text

items.title: Claude Code adapter: spawn, attach, inject and state

criteria.text: From the Neovim client, a human message in General reaches a real Claude Code session; the stage shows `injected` once the mod submits it; the reply appears in the thread

The session's state changes are visible in the hub (`busy` during a turn, `idle` after, `waiting for approval` on a permission prompt) and come from hooks or the mod, never from the model's self-report
`attach_command` returns a command that, run in a terminal, attaches to the live session; two attached clients work
After a hub restart, `resume` re-finds the running session through the process table and reconnects state reporting
The capability table declares what the adapter cannot do (for example approval relay) instead of emulating it
Tests drive the adapter against a fake Claude Code (a fake harness process honouring the hooks and the mod surface); one manual smoke run against the real harness is recorded in the ticket

items.title: Workbench shell in Neovim

criteria.text: `cland` from the repo root opens the workbench on General with the Claude Code session visible in the sessions panel; Enter attaches it in the centre; `:restart` re-attaches rather than kills it
Panels toggle with the keys of `WORKBENCH.md`; pressing the active right-panel key hides the panel; the state line always names the centre view
Shift+Enter inserts a newline in the composer and reaches a harness TUI in a terminal buffer as the kitty CSI-u sequence; pasting text with tabs into a terminal buffer keeps the tabs
No hit-enter prompt can be triggered by hub events; UI updates land while the user is typing
Headless tests drive the shell with `nvim_input` and assert `screenstring()` for each panel toggle and view switch against a stub hub over stdio

items.title: Codex adapter

criteria.text: A Codex session spawned from the hub appears in the registry with its state; a message to it from General is `injected` and its reply comes back
`attach_command` opens the real Codex TUI on the hub-owned thread; a Neovim restart leaves the thread running
No `-c` override or `--profile` is ever passed to the Codex TUI process
State transitions `idle` → `active` → `waiting for approval` → `idle` are observed from the app-server, not inferred
Tests run against a fake Codex app-server speaking JSON-RPC on a Unix socket; one manual smoke run against the real harness is recorded

items.title: OpenCode adapter

criteria.text: An OpenCode session spawned from the hub receives a General message as `injected` and replies into the thread
The capability table marks `waiting for human` as heuristic and the UI shows that qualifier
`attach_command` opens the OpenCode TUI on the hub's session; the session survives a Neovim restart
A pending permission in OpenCode shows as `waiting for approval` in the hub within one event
Tests run against a fake OpenCode server (HTTP plus SSE); one manual smoke run against the real harness with a free model is recorded

items.title: Session launcher and the sessions panel

criteria.text: Launching Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions from the UI works with the model chosen at launch; each appears in the panel with live state
Enter attaches the selected session in the centre; `C-v` attaches in a split; `x` stops it after confirmation
The panel shows `unknown` for a session whose process died and a journal event is written
The picker's sessions kind filters by name, role and harness and attaches on Enter
Headless tests cover launch, attach command resolution, stop and the capability display against fake harnesses

items.title: Roles config and clause delivery

criteria.text: Assigning a role delivers its clause to the session as a hub event; the journal shows the delivery; a reconnect of the session delivers it again
A second Coordinator assignment is refused with a reason; revoking the only Coordinator shows the vacancy warning within one event
A session launched for a role uses the role's launch defaults from `roles.toml`; editing the file changes the next launch
The sessions panel, the picker and the top bar show the role with the name
Tests cover assignment, exclusivity, clause redelivery on reconnect and the vacancy warning against fake harnesses

items.title: Hub permissions by role and the audit log

criteria.text: A refused call returns a typed error naming the missing permission; the UI shows it in the Agents topic
Every call, allowed or refused, appears in the journal with session, role, tool and outcome
Changing a session's role changes its permissions on the next call without a reconnect
Tests exercise every row of the table for every role with a real hub and scripted spokes

items.title: Role handover with a note

criteria.text: A handover from session A to session B moves the Coordinator role atomically: B receives clause plus note, A receives "role revoked", the Agents topic shows both events
A handover without a note from the Coordinator is refused; from the human it is allowed
After the handover, B's `history` and the role-state query return the topics waiting for an agent and the claims held by the role
Tests cover handover, refusal without a note, revocation mid-turn and the state pull against fake harnesses

items.title: Topic model: statuses, bindings, creation and mentions

criteria.text: Status follows direction: a human message sets `waiting for agent`, an agent reply sets `open`; `resolve` clears a wait
`@reviewer` in a message reaches the session holding Reviewer and its reply appears in the same topic; `@name` reaches that session
A message to a vacant Coordinator is queued and delivered when a Coordinator is assigned; the topic shows the warning meanwhile
An agent-created topic requires a title; a second topic for the same unit of work is refused
The topics panel and picker show statuses, unread counts and pinning as in the design; headless tests assert the screen

items.title: Asks and the inbox

criteria.text: Only a session holding Coordinator can post an ask; others are refused with a typed error
Answering with `2` from the inbox posts the answer with `answer_to`, clears the topic's wait and removes the row; the thread shows the answer under the card
A session entering `waiting for approval` appears under approvals within one event and disappears when the state changes; Enter attaches it
Notifications dismiss with `d` and `D` and never block anything; asks and approvals cannot be dismissed
The "needs you" count equals asks plus approvals plus waiting topics; headless tests assert the inbox sections and the count

items.title: Agents topic, journal and hygiene

criteria.text: Two sessions exchanging messages show up in Agents with sender, role and time; the human's own topics show nothing of it
A looping pair trips the breaker at the configured threshold, both see a typed refusal, the Agents topic shows the mute, and the mute survives a hub restart
Changing a threshold in `config.toml` takes effect on the next hub start
The journal file contains every event and audit line as JSON lines and is append-only across restarts
Tests cover the breaker, persistence of mutes and the Agents view against a real hub

items.title: Tracker items as files with the hub index and the cland task CLI

criteria.text: `cland task create` writes a file with the frontmatter and a sequential id; `cland task list --state open --label x` queries the index
Editing a file by hand updates the index within a second; a concurrent hub write and hand edit end with the last writer's content and a journal note
`cland task claim T-12` records a claim in the hub without touching the file; `cland task view T-12` shows both assignee and claim
A verdict comment with the structured header is stored in the file and queryable through the index (`cland task list --verdict review=clear`)
Tests drive the CLI against a real hub in a temporary project and assert on the files and the index

items.title: Items panel, item view and board

criteria.text: The tree reflects the files within a second of a change; filters and the map grouping match the design's rules
From an item, `gt` opens its topic (creating none; the topic appears when the first message about the item arrives) and `gs` attaches the claiming session; from a topic, `gi` opens the bound item
The board's columns derive from state, claims and verdicts without a stored workflow status
Headless tests assert the panel, the view and the board text for a fixture set of items against a real hub

items.title: Skills on the own tracker

criteria.text: `to-tickets` run in a test project creates items with parent and blocked-by edges in `.cland/tasks` through `cland task`
`wayfinder` creates a map item and child items, claims through the assignee and finds the frontier through the CLI
`triage` applies the configured labels through `cland task edit`
Every patch to a vendored skill is listed in a `skills/PATCHES.md` note with the reason
The `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` template is the one `cland init` will provision

items.title: Migration of GitHub Issues into .cland/tasks

criteria.text: Importing a test repository with sub-issues and blocked-by edges reproduces parent and `blocked_by` in the frontmatter and the comments in the files
Re-running the import changes nothing when GitHub has not changed
Run once on the cland repo: every open issue has an item, and `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` on `main` describes `cland task`
The run and its counts are recorded in a comment on this ticket

items.title: cland init and managed files

criteria.text: `cland init` on an empty repo and on a repo with its own `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/settings.json` leaves user content intact and adds only managed parts
Running `cland init` twice changes nothing; `cland update` after a version bump rewrites only managed parts
A session launched in the initialised project reads the generic instructions from `AGENTS.md` under all three harnesses (Claude Code through the import when `CLAUDE.md` exists)
`git status` after init shows only the committed set (`tasks/`, `roles.toml`, `config.toml`, `.gitignore`, skills, docs, `AGENTS.md`, hooks)
Tests run init and update on fixture repos and diff the results

items.title: cland doctor

criteria.text: On a healthy machine every check passes; removing the hub's discovery file or breaking the skills symlink produces a named failure with the fix
A harness version outside the tested range is reported as a warning, not a failure
The output is plain text suitable for pasting into an item comment
Tests fake each failure condition and assert the report

items.title: Review and QA through the roles

criteria.text: A review request from the Coordinator reaches a real Codex session holding Reviewer; its verdict comment lands on the item with the structured header; the item view shows "review clear" or "not clear"
The same for QA with astra, including one headless Neovim check in its run
A verdict written by a session not holding the role is refused by the hub
The fallback path through `/codex:rescue` is documented in the Reviewer and QA clauses and tried once
The run is recorded in a comment on this ticket with the item used

items.title: Dogfooding: the first real cland task inside cland

criteria.text: One real item of the cland project is taken from claim to verdicts entirely inside cland, with the three harnesses in their roles
At least one ask was raised by the Coordinator and answered from the inbox; at least one role handover or reconnect happened without losing the thread
Every blocker found is either fixed in this ticket or filed as an item with a link here
The human confirms in a comment that cland replaced the previous set of tools for that task

items.title: cland inbox and cland topic answer: answer an ask from the CLI
cland CLI: find the hub from a worktree of the project
spoke session.launch: accept cwd, so the Coordinator can launch a session in a worktree
OpenCode: a deprecated default free model fails every turn, and the failure is silent
Session usage: a running total per session, the same meaning for every adapter
Codex sessions launched by cland: approvals auto-approved and a per-role sandbox, so no check or commit waits on the human
cland CLI with a session identity: the hub refuses the human-only commands
A message injected into a Codex session in the last second of its turn is marked injected but never acted on
A Codex session's spoke replaced with no attach behind it: the session's tool calls then fail silently until a stop and relaunch
OpenCode launch with no model on a cold catalog picks the first listed free model before the Zen models arrive
Codex Implementer and QA sessions run with full access by default: any work a role needs, on any harness
Under load the items tree reverted to an earlier snapshot after live updates: a late full list overwriting newer events?
Codex redelivery (T-50) fires on every delivery to an idle session: the thread check reads userMessage items only, and hub_event tool outputs never match
The test harness takes a machine-wide lock before spawning daemons, runs the hub suite at bounded concurrency, and kills its daemons on failure
Orphan harness servers and hub daemons: session stop ends the server, doctor and hub start sweep what no session owns
The Coordinator's tracker and docs commits have no sanctioned path to the territory's dev: the hook refuses them, and the only workaround is the raw marker
Shared synchronous I/O on every hub request: the permission check reads roles.toml and the journal writes with writeSync
Orphan sweep misses the live app-server of a session recorded as exited
Tracker writes on hub request paths still use synchronous fs: item commits in Tracker's atomic write
Merge, worktree and release checks still read items through the tracker's synchronous view
Harness adapters do synchronous fs while spawning a session: Codex mkdirSync, rmSync, openSync and closeSync on launch
Items panel: the "in work" filter hides items between review and QA and planned items
